metadata.description: Municipal law, administrative organization, electoral law, and environmental legislation

laws.official_number: Legislative Decree No. 118 of June 30, 1977 (Municipal Act)

amendments.summary: Major amendments to the Municipal Act. Key reform of municipal governance and elections.

laws.historical_context: Primary law governing Lebanon's 1,064 municipalities. Enacted during the early civil war period. Defines municipal powers, elections, budgets, and relationship with central government. Article 16 states that parliamentary election provisions apply to municipal elections. Municipal elections are held separately from parliamentary elections. Municipalities manage local affairs including urban planning, waste management, local roads, and public spaces. Lebanon also has 51 municipal unions (federations of municipalities).

Governs the office of moukhtar (مختار), the elected neighborhood/village chief. Lebanon has 3,018 moukhtars who serve as local administrative officials handling personal status documentation, attestations, and acting as intermediaries between citizens and government agencies.

laws.official_title_arabic: قانون انتخاب أعضاء مجلس النواب - قانون رقم 44/2017
laws.official_title_french: Loi No. 44/2017 - Élection des Membres du Parlement

amendments.summary: Suspended biometric voting card (Art. 84) and diaspora constituency (Arts. 112, 122) for 2022 elections on exceptional one-time basis. Rescheduled election date.

laws.historical_context: Replaced Electoral Law No. 25/2008. Landmark reform: introduced proportional representation for the first time in Lebanese history (replacing winner-takes-all majoritarian system). Key features: 15 electoral districts, preferential voting within party lists, diaspora voting provisions (Article 3), establishment of Supervisory Commission for Elections, campaign finance regulations including lifting banking secrecy for campaign accounts. The law was used for the 2018 and 2022 parliamentary elections. Previous electoral laws: Law 25/2008, Law 171/2000, Law of 1960.

laws.official_number: Law No. 216 of April 2, 1993 (Urban Planning / Construction)

amendments.summary: Comprehensive amendments to building regulations and permits.

laws.historical_context: Governs building permits, construction standards, zoning, and urban planning regulations. Administered by the Directorate General of Urban Planning (DGU) and the Order of Engineers and Architects. Post-war reconstruction generated significant construction activity, making this law particularly important.

Lebanon's primary environmental legislation. Established the Ministry of Environment's mandate, environmental impact assessment requirements, pollution control standards, and nature protection provisions. Implementation has been criticized as weak due to institutional capacity constraints.

laws.official_number: Law No. 462 of September 2, 2002 (Council for Development & Reconstruction)
laws.official_title_french: Loi sur le Conseil de Développement et de Reconstruction (CDR)
laws.official_title_english: Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR) Law
laws.historical_context: Established the CDR as the primary government body for physical infrastructure reconstruction and development project management. Originally created in 1977 for post-war reconstruction, it became the main conduit for international development funding to Lebanon.

laws.official_number: Law No. 28 of February 11, 2017 (Access to Information)
laws.official_title_arabic: قانون الحق في الوصول إلى المعلومات - قانون رقم 28/2017
laws.official_title_french: Loi No. 28/2017 - Droit d'Accès à l'Information
laws.historical_context: Landmark transparency legislation granting citizens the right to access information held by government entities. Requires proactive publication of certain categories of information. Establishes procedures for information requests and exemptions. Implementation has been gradual, with the National Anti-Corruption Commission taking on oversight responsibilities.

laws.official_number: Law No. 175 of May 8, 2020 (Anti-Corruption / National Anti-Corruption Commission)
laws.official_title_arabic: قانون مكافحة الفساد في القطاع العام وإنشاء الهيئة الوطنية لمكافحة الفساد
laws.official_title_french: Loi No. 175/2020 - Lutte contre la Corruption
laws.official_title_english: Anti-Corruption in the Public Sector and Establishment of the National Anti-Corruption Commission Law
laws.historical_context: Established the National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC) and criminalized corruption in the public sector. Part of a package of reform laws demanded by the international community. The NACC was eventually formed in 2022 after delays in appointing commissioners.

laws.official_title_arabic: قانون حماية كاشفي الفساد - قانون رقم 189/2020
laws.official_title_french: Loi No. 189/2020 - Protection des Dénonciateurs de Corruption
laws.historical_context: Provides legal protections for individuals who report corruption in the public and private sectors. Covers protection from retaliation, confidentiality guarantees, and procedures for reporting.

laws.official_title_french: Loi Ottomane de 1909 sur les Associations et Décret 2791/1959
laws.historical_context: One of the oldest still-operative laws in Lebanon, dating from the Ottoman period (1909). Governs the formation and operation of non-profit associations, clubs, and civil society organizations. Requires notification (ilm wa khabar) to the Ministry of Interior for formation. Despite its age, the law provides a relatively permissive framework for civil society. Decree 2791/1959 supplemented Ottoman-era provisions. The law also governs political parties, which has been criticized as outdated.
